items.ncert_ref: Section 8.3 - Figure it Out Q11, Fig. 8.7 (book p.198; LP numbering Q2)
items.question_text: A colony of ants set out in search of food. As they search, they keep splitting equally at each point and reach two food sources, one near a mango tree and another near a sugarcane field. What fraction of the original group reached each food source? (At the first split the group goes half to a path to the mango tree and half upwards. The second split sends half of that group to the mango tree and half upwards. The third split sends the group into four equal parts: two go to the mango tree, one goes to the sugarcane field and one goes upwards. The last split sends half to the mango tree and half to the sugarcane field.)
items.reason: Printed answer (p.39) is text only (29/32 and 3/32). The same diagram with the fraction of the original group written on every path (1/2, 1/2; 1/4, 1/4; four of 1/16; 1/32, 1/32) and the totals 29/32 and 3/32 would help but is not needed: not added.

items.question_text: A miser gave a beggar 1/5 of 1/16 of 1/4 of 1/2 of 2/3 of 3/4 of a dramma. If 1 dramma equals 1280 cowrie shells, how many cowrie shells did the beggar get?
items.reason: A product of six fractions, 6/7680 = 1/1280 and 1280 x 1/1280 = 1; the book prints no figure for the miser's problem.
